CC - Back pain with leg weakness.

HPI - 66-year-old man with history of prostate cancer who presents with 2 weeks of worsening mid-thoracic back pain, now with bilateral leg weakness and numbness below the nipple line. He reports urinary retention for 1 day. No fever, no trauma. Prostate cancer diagnosed 3 years ago, treated with radiation; last PSA 6 months ago was rising.

PMH - Prostate adenocarcinoma, hypertension.

Meds - Leuprolide injection q3months; Amlodipine 10 mg daily; Oxycodone 10 mg q6h PRN pain.

SH - Retired veteran. No tobacco. Rare alcohol.

ROS - Back pain, weakness, numbness, urinary retention as above. Denies bowel incontinence.

Exam -
VS: T 98.4 F, HR 92, BP 150/90, RR 16, SpO2 97% RA.
Spine: Mid-thoracic tenderness, no step-off.
Neuro: Bilateral lower extremity weakness 3/5, sensory level at T6, hyperreflexia, Babinski positive bilaterally. Rectal tone decreased.

Data -
Labs: PSA 48 (H), Ca 11.2 (H), Creatinine 1.4 (H), Hgb 11.2.
MRI thoracic spine: T5 vertebral body lesion with epidural extension and severe cord compression.

A - 66-year-old man with prostate cancer and MRI-confirmed malignant spinal cord compression at T5.

P -
1. Malignant spinal cord compression
- STAT dexamethasone 10 mg IV
- Neurosurgery and radiation oncology consults emergently
- Strict bed rest, log-roll precautions
2. Hypercalcemia
- IV fluids, calcitonin; consider bisphosphonate
- Recheck calcium q12h
3. Urinary retention
- Foley catheter placed; monitor output
